rv.q: This affecting King Lear variation suggests she has a genuinely fresh perspective—warm and wise but also tough-minded and wickedly funny—to bring to depictions of the Asian-American experience in theater.

Laowang is the kind of play you can pick at endlessly -- the author, Alex Lin, tosses a little of everything into a tumultuous ninety minutes -- but you can't mistake its vigor, comic energy, and knack for surprise revelations.
In practice, though, the production fails to live up to the premise or offer any real insight into these characters.
Lin is certainly a talented playwright, and Laowang is a wonderful introduction.
The dialogue, stylishly delivered by a first-rate cast, is witty, urbane, and frequently arch.
